full_judgment: 8. Thus, from the aforesaid observation it seems to me that in this case the conviction of other accused persons is also based on the confessional statement of the petitioner No. 1 Hakim Ali. Normally in a case of dacoity the question of recognition is of great importance. In this case on reference to the evidence I myself do not find that there is anything before the learned Court below to show that except the petitioner No. 1 any of the witnesses recognized the other petitioners as dacoits committing the dacoity in this case. Mr. Barua also could not show that there was any evidence to support conviction of Liton, Abdul Khaleque and Chiku. Merely on the basis of a confessional statement of a co-accused without any corroborative evidence by any independent eye-witness it is unsafe to convict a person under section 395 of the Penal Code. It has been found by both the Courts below that the confessional statement made by Hakim Ali was true and voluntary. In the instant case taking into consideration the evidence and the surrounding circumstances conviction of Hakim Ali under section 395 has been legally upheld. But his conviction under section 412 of the Penal Code for dishonestly receiving the television which was the subject matter or commission of the dacoity cannot be separately made as the offence of receiving the television constitutes a distinct offence out of the same act of dacoity. Mr. Barua also submits that conviction under section 412 of the Penal Code in this case is illegal. The conviction of Hakim Ali under section 412 of the Penal Code is set aside but his conviction under section 395 of the Code is upheld. The conviction of the other 3 accused petitioners namely, Liton, Abdul Khaleque and Chiku are set aside as conviction of these persons cannot be sustained merely on the basis of the confessional statement of the co-accused Hakim Ali without any corroborative evidence. Before I part with the judgment, I must observe that the learned Sessions Judge convicted accused Liton, Abdul Khaleque and Chiku drawing an adverse presumption against them most illegally. Rather it is a settled principle of criminal jurisprudence that there is always a presumption of innocence in favour of the accused. It is unfortunate that the learned Sessions Judge made the aforesaid observation which can be made a basis for convicting the other petitioners in this case. Accordingly, I find Liton, Abdul Khaleque and Chiku not guilty of the offence under section 395 as the prosecution failed to prove its case beyond any reasonable doubt against those accused persons and I acquit them of the charge under section 395. The accused petitioners Liton, Abdul Khaleque and Chiku are released from their bail bond.
